title: Adverse events associated with unblinded, but not with blinded, statin therapy in the Anglo-Scandinavian Cardiac Outcomes Trial-Lipid-Lowering Arm (ASCOT-LLA): a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial and its non-randomised non-blind extension phase
authors: Gupta A, Thompson D, Whitehouse A, Collier T, Dahlof B, Poulter N, et al.
followUp: blinded phase median 3.3 years; non-blinded phase median 2.3 years
population: Patients aged 40 to 79 with hypertension, at least three other cardiovascular risk factors and total cholesterol 6.5 mmol/L or lower; 9899 in the non-randomised open-label extension (6409 atorvastatin users, 3490 non-users)
funder: Pfizer, Servier Research Group, and Leo Laboratories (summary). The full funding statement and the role of the funders were not read.
result: Blinded phase, atorvastatin 10 mg (n=5101) against placebo (n=5079): muscle-related adverse events 298 (2.03% per annum) against 283 (2.00%), HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.88 to 1.21); erectile dysfunction 1.86% against 2.14% per annum; sleep disturbance 1.00% against 1.46% per annum (HR 0.69); cognitive impairment 31 against 32 reports, too few for reliable analysis; renal and urinary adverse events 481 (1.87% per annum) against 392 (1.51%), HR 1.23 (1.08 to 1.41). Non-blinded phase: muscle-related adverse events 161 (1.26% per annum) in statin users against 124 (1.00%) in non-users, HR 1.41 (1.10 to 1.79); musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders 8.69% against 7.45% per annum (HR 1.17); blood and lymphatic disorders 0.88% against 0.64% per annum (HR 1.40). The authors attribute the excess in the non-blinded phase to a nocebo effect. Published correspondence noted that the overall proportion reporting muscle-related events was lower in the non-blinded phase than in the blinded phase.
